title: Embedded SDK fallback matrix and canonical playbook
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Purpose
-------
This playbook documents a canonical fallback matrix for Redwood embedded SDKs and a reproducible triage + remediation workflow for the most frequent customer-visible failure modes. It is intended for developer-experience engineers, support engineers, and SREs who need a deterministic path from alert -> mitigation -> long-term fix.

Scope
-----
- Applies to: Embedded and local SDK integrations (JS/TS, Python, and light-weight mobile wrappers) that call Redwood hosted or dedicated endpoints.
- Excludes: Private on-prem runtime packaging steps for air-gapped installs (see eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging).

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Primary owner: devx-observability (team lead: Asha Patel)
- Secondary: eng-sre on-call for platform impacts
- Support escalation: follow the normal support-handoff runbook; for P1s notify SRE within 15 minutes.

How to use this document
------------------------
1. Use the matrix below to map symptoms to a recommended immediate fallback.
2. Execute the short remediation steps in the Incident TL;DR section.
3. Run the reproducible test in the Repro and Golden Trace section.
4. Patch, validate in canary, and schedule a follow-up RCA + regression test.

Fallback decision matrix (quick reference)
-----------------------------------------
Symptom | Probable cause | Immediate fallback | Severity | Owner
--------|----------------|--------------------|----------|------
Partial tokens / truncated streams | Client-side network stalls or stream abort | Switch to polling mode; increase client-side stream timeout to 60s | Medium | devx-support
Very high latency (end-to-end > 2x SLO) | Runtime hot-node or queueing | Route to cheaper warm replica model (fallback model ID: rdm-lite-1) and enable prefix-caching | High | eng-sre
Incorrect structured output (schema violations) | Prompt/SDK serializer mismatch | Switch to stable schema mode (v2025-schema) and enable strict validation flag | Medium | devx
Authentication errors (401/403) | Key rotation or KMS policy change | Temporarily allow tenant-scoped read-only API keys and trigger credential re-issue flow | High | security
Token cost spike without corresponding traffic | Client inadvertently enabling full context retention | Force local context-prune and enable sampling-based prompt bundling | Medium | product-eng
Model fallback produced degraded content quality | Fallback model quantization mismatch | Use model-agnostic postfilter (quality-gate v1) and route small fraction to golden model for diffing | Medium | applied-ml

Incident TL;DR (actions for first 15/60/240 minutes)
---------------------------------------------------
- First 15 minutes (Detect & Stabilize):
  1. Acknowledge the incident in PagerDuty and tag with product:embedded-sdk.
  2. Confirm scope: sample 5 traces across different tenants.
  3. If customers are impacted, switch affected SDKs to the recommended immediate fallback listed in the matrix.
  4. Capture a golden trace (see Repro section).
- First 60 minutes (Mitigate & Communicate):
  1. Open a dedicated Slack incident channel and post status every 15 minutes.
  2. Apply a short-lived hotfix (roll forward) to the SDK or routing rules as required.
  3. If routing change, validate error rate and latency for 5–10 minutes before notifying customers.
- First 4 hours (Restore & Begin RCA):
  1. Confirm functional restore across all affected tenants.
  2. Begin root cause collection (logs, heap/CPU profiles, kernel traces if runtime).
  3. Create follow-up Jira with mitigation, owners, and ETA for permanent fix.

Repro and Golden Trace instructions
----------------------------------
- Goal: produce a deterministic trace that demonstrates the failure across client + network + runtime.
- Steps to reproduce locally:
  1. Acquire an impacted API key (test tenant or redwood-internal sandbox).
  2. Set SDK env var REDWOOD_SDK_LOG_LEVEL=debug and REDWOOD_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=30s.
  3. Capture a streaming session with curl or local harness:
     - Example (curl streaming):
       curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"<problematic input>\",\"max_tokens\":512}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embedded/generate
  4. Save client-side network dump (Wireshark/tcpdump), SDK debug logs, and the server trace id returned in headers (x-rw-trace-id).
- Golden trace: tag the trace with label \"golden:embedded:failure\" in the tracing system and upload artifacts to the incident Jira.

Canonical fixes (ranked by breadth & permanence)
------------------------------------------------
- Fix A: SDK serializer/validator patch (low-risk)
  - When to use: schema and serialization mismatches.
  - Steps: update SDK to use Schema v2025, add strict-mode opt-in, publish patch release with changelog.
  - Validation: run schema-golden-suite across 1000 prompts.
- Fix B: Routing policy temporary pin (medium-risk)
  - When to use: runtime node pressure or model-quality regressions.
  - Steps: pin traffic to warm pool, reduce batch size from 16 -> 8 for 30 minutes, enable model-agnostic postfilter.
  - Validation: compare token latency and cost delta pre/post.
- Fix C: Runtime kernel micro-patch (high-risk)
  - When to use: deterministic kernel crash or memory leak.
  - Steps: prepare canary image, run smoke bench for 1 hour, then deploy to 10% traffic with auto-rollback.
  - Validation: heap + GPU memory stable for 2 hours and no regressions in tail latency.

Telemetry checklist (what to check first)
--------------------------------------
- SDK metrics: call rate, stream aborts, local queue size, client-side timeouts.
- Platform metrics: per-model latency P50/P95/P99, queue length, GPU memory utilization per node.
- Trace sampling: confirm x-rw-trace-id exists and maps across client -> edge -> runtime.
- Cost signals: token count per user-session and token cost deltas.

Rollback and canary guidance
---------------------------
- Canary policy for SDK patches: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15-minute observation windows.
- Rollback triggers: P95 latency increase > 30% OR error rate increase > 2% over baseline.
- When routing changes, always enable traffic mirror to old path for 10 minutes for offline comparison.

Post-incident actions and tests to add to CI
-------------------------------------------
- Add a golden-trace regression test: replay captured golden traces against the new SDK release in CI.
- Add an integration test that toggles fallback policies and asserts no correctness regressions under 3 simulated network profiles.
- Schedule an applied-ml QA run for model fallback quality when new quantized variants are onboarded.

Frequently seen root causes and canonical remediation mapping
-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Client-side timeouts and stream buffering -> Increase client timeouts, switch to polling, and publish SDK guidance.
2. Model variant mismatch after rollout -> Immediate routing pin to previous model, diff-runner, and notify model-onboarding.
3. Key/credential rotation mismatch -> Short-lived allowlist and force re-issue; add SDK-friendly key refresh helpers.
4. Unexpected token inflation from prompt accumulation -> Enforce per-session token budget and add client TTL-based context pruning.

Appendix A: Example SDK patch commands
-------------------------------------
- Patch, build, and publish (JS/TS):
  1. git checkout -b fix/serializer-strict
  2. npm run test:unit && npm run build && npm run test:integration
  3. npm version patch && npm publish --tag canary
  4. Update docs site with migration note and sample diff.
- Patch, build, and publish (Python):
  1. git checkout -b fix/serializer-strict
  2. tox -e py && pytest tests/integration
  3. python setup.py sdist bdist_wheel && twine upload --repository-url testpypi dist/*

Appendix B: Quick reference config table
---------------------------------------
| Setting | Default | Recommended for failure | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------------------------|-------|
| REDWOOD_CLIENT_TIMEOUT | 20s | 60s | Prevents early client aborts |
| REDWOOD_SDK_VALIDATE_SCHEMA | false | true (strict) | Use when schema mismatches observed |
| FALLBACK_MODEL_ID | rdm-default | rdm-lite-1 | rdm-lite-1 is lower-cost and more robust under pressure |
| PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED | true | true | Ensure prefix cache size >= 128k entries for embedded workloads |
